newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard sees Q3 loss, cites fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard sees Q3 loss, cites fuel costs.

text.p: Vanguard Airlines Inc said Monday it expects to show a loss for the third quarter ended September 30, 1996.

"Adverse publicity surrounding the TWA crash, higher fuel costs, reinstatement of the 10 percent federal ticket tax and slow traffic in September contributed to the third quarter loss," said Bob McAdoo, chairman and chief executive officer of Vanguard, in a statement.
McAdoo said the company is working on plans to improve operations in the fourth quarter including reducing service in unprofitable markets and commencing service in new markets.

Vanguard began service from Cincinnati to Chicago-Midway and Kansas City on October 1 and service from Kansas City to Seattle on October 10, and will begin service to Phoenix from several cities as early as October 17.

He said recent actions by one of Vanguard's competitors in the company's new and existing markets may have a substantially negative impact on Vanguard's fourth quarter and may force the carrier to modify its current route structure.
Vanguard reported a 1996 second quarter loss of $1.9 million or $0.23 a share on revenues of $20.7 million.

Depending on the size of the third quarter loss, Vanguard said it may not meet the net worth requirements for continued listing on the Nasdaq SmallCap Stock Market. If the company's common stock is not listed on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market, trading in the company's common stock will be conducted on the OTC Bulletin Board or in the over-the-counter market.

Vanguard, which began service in December 1994 and is headquartered in Kansas City, is a low-price, short- to medium-haul passenger airline providing scheduled jet service to 12 cities throughout the West, Rocky Mountains and Midwest.
The carrier currently employs 568 people and operates a fleet of eight aircraft, consisting of two Boeing 737-300s and six Boeing 737-200s.
Shares of Vanguard closed at 5-1/4 on October 10.
